rationale: Existing tests cover several supporting behaviors, but the current Crafting Profit screen still performs a fixed account-then-TP refresh and its response type has no freshness envelope. The new lifecycle checks below are needed to verify the story’s envelope-driven behavior independently. No new test files were added because the current frontend contract lacks the fields and lifecycle needed to express those checks without either duplicating existing cases or producing compile-only failures; the specifications are precise enough to implement with the story.

acceptance_checks.criterion: AC1: Show usable provisional cached results while refresh runs; show loading/empty for 202 with no usable result.
acceptance_checks.expected: A successful provisional response renders its supplied rows immediately with the stale-data indicator and explanation. A 202 response without rows shows loading/pending and never fabricates a row.
acceptance_checks.verification: Frontend component test using controlled calculation responses and deferred task completion; assert row values and visible state before releasing tasks.

acceptance_checks.criterion: AC2: Poll advertised task references and resubmit using current settings until required account and TP inputs are fresh.
acceptance_checks.expected: Task success alone does not end recovery. The client resubmits and follows any further account or TP work advertised by the backend; the indicator ends only after rendering the final current-context result.
acceptance_checks.verification: Component integration test with controlled HTTP client and clock covering provisional-to-final, 202-to-result, successive insufficient-scope account work, and TP work required after account inputs change.

acceptance_checks.criterion: AC3: Preserve controls and correlate calculation, task, and detail responses.
acceptance_checks.expected: Replacement keeps current settings, filters, sort and still-valid row selection; missing selections fall back gracefully. Late task, calculation, or detail responses cannot replace newer context, and detail is associated with the matching provisional row context.
acceptance_checks.verification: Deferred-response component regressions for settings changes, reordered responses, changed/removed selection, and detail tied to an older calculation; assert the displayed row and detail remain context-compatible.

acceptance_checks.criterion: AC4: Bound automatic recovery to five cumulative minutes and expose safe failure/retry.
acceptance_checks.expected: Polling, successive tasks, and recalculations share one deadline. Unknown/expired tasks, transport errors, task failure, and deadline exhaustion stop animation and retain last usable rows with retry; no-cache failure is explicit. Retry starts a new bounded cycle without assuming cancellation or overlapping writes.
acceptance_checks.verification: Controlled-clock and transport component tests for cumulative deadline across task changes, unknown task, transport failure, failure with and without cached rows, and explicit retry.

acceptance_checks.criterion: AC5: Preserve backend values and distinguish account and TP freshness.
acceptance_checks.expected: Rendered monetary values, states, and resolution quantities exactly match deliberately non-derivable backend fixture values. Account and TP status remain separately represented; ordinary Profit refresh does not require a System Status visit.
acceptance_checks.verification: Component/API contract checks using independent fixtures with totals that differ from arithmetic derivations; assert supplied values and separate freshness indicators.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Browser acceptance: prove the controlled stale/failure lifecycle in a real browser and separately verify the delivered backend envelope connection.
acceptance_checks.expected: Built page visibly renders cached rows, indicator, preserved controls, safe detail association, and bounded termination under deterministic controlled responses; a separate check confirms the browser receives the delivered backend envelope.
acceptance_checks.verification: Extend/run the focused Profit browser smoke against controlled responses for stale and failure states, then run a separate backend-envelope connection check. Record prerequisites and limitations; neither check substitutes for real-data performance acceptance.

invariants: The browser presents backend monetary values, domain states, and quantities unchanged and performs no crafting calculation.
A task's successful state is not evidence that all required account sources or TP IDs are fresh.
Only a final calculation for the current request/settings/context removes the provisional indicator.
No result rows are fabricated when the backend reports 202 without usable cached data.
Detail must explain the same compatible row/calculation context currently displayed.
One five-minute deadline covers the entire automatic recovery cycle; starting further tasks does not reset it.
A client timeout does not imply backend cancellation and must not create overlapping writes.
Account-source freshness and TP coverage remain independently visible.
existing_tests_reviewed: frontend/src/crafting/__tests__/CraftingProfitScreen.spec.ts — loading/empty/error states, explicit reload, selection removal, stale calculation ordering, and preserving search/sort/selection through reload.
frontend/src/crafting/__tests__/profitResolutionAssociation.spec.ts — correlates detail to recipe and effective calculation inputs and ignores superseded detail responses.
frontend/src/crafting/__tests__/useProfitTableView.spec.ts — preserves table-view state and uses supplied totals for sorting.
frontend/src/crafting/__tests__/SelectedResultDetail.spec.ts — renders supplied detail monetary values and full-quantity semantics.
frontend/src/api/__tests__/syncApi.spec.ts — trigger acceptance and task-status response contract, including HTTP 202 task acceptance.
frontend/src/api/__tests__/http.spec.ts — existing advertised-task wait/retry behavior for account freshness errors.
frontend/scripts/profit-browser-smoke.mjs — real-browser controlled-origin layout/interaction smoke; current script does not establish UD-015 stale/failure lifecycle behavior.
test_specifications: In a Crafting Profit component test, return a successful provisional response whose fixture totals differ from its component values, hold the advertised task pending, and assert immediately that supplied rows and values are visible with the stale explanation. Complete the task, return a final response, and assert the indicator disappears only after that replacement renders.

Return 202 with freshness/task metadata and no rows; while pending assert loading/empty presentation and zero fabricated table rows. After task completion return usable calculation data and assert it renders.

Script backend freshness checks so one account task completes but leaves required sources stale, then a successive account task and TP task are advertised. Assert each advertised task is polled, calculation is resubmitted with current settings, and task success alone does not remove the indicator.

During a provisional refresh, change settings and table controls, then resolve older task/calculation responses after the newer context. Assert the latest context/settings and response values remain visible, with filters/sort and valid selection preserved.

Resolve a detail request from newer inputs while an older provisional row remains displayed. Assert it is not shown as that row's explanation; after the matching replacement row arrives, assert only its associated detail appears.

With a controlled clock, consume most of the five-minute budget across polling and successive task/recalculation steps; verify the deadline is cumulative, terminates recovery, stops animation, and retains last usable rows. Repeat failure cases for unknown task and transport rejection with cached rows and without cached rows.
After bounded failure, click retry and assert a fresh bounded cycle rechecks backend freshness, does not presume prior work was cancelled, and does not launch overlapping account writes.

Use independent row and detail fixtures with totals intentionally inconsistent with multiplication of parts; assert displayed monetary values, states, and resolution quantities equal backend values, and that account and TP freshness remain separately identifiable.

Run the focused real-browser Profit smoke on the built bundle with a controlled origin and scripted provisional/failure responses. Assert visible rows and indicator, preservation of controls, matching detail association, and safe termination. Separately verify a browser request reaches the delivered backend envelope; document that controlled-origin checks do not prove real-data timing.

post_implementation_review_reason: Required because this changes a critical asynchronous recovery and result/detail association flow; review the prepared deterministic lifecycle tests, five-minute cumulative deadline evidence, browser controlled-response evidence, and separate backend-envelope connection evidence.

post_implementation_reviews.reason: The implementation covers provisional results, envelope-driven recovery, and the reported browser and backend-envelope checks. However, the cumulative deadline is checked only between awaited requests: a pending task-status or calculation request can keep recovery animating past five minutes, and a late calculation response can still be applied. The deadline regression uses immediately resolving requests, so it does not cover this case.
evidence: The prepared lifecycle test file is present and includes coverage for provisional and pending responses, task sequencing, response correlation, failure and retry, and a cumulative deadline across successive tasks.

In useCraftingProfit.ts, recover() awaits sendProfit() and awaitTask() without enforcing the remaining deadline during those requests. sendProfit() applies a response when its request ID is current, without checking whether its recovery cycle has expired.
The cumulative deadline test advances a controlled clock through rounds with immediately resolving task and calculation responses; it does not advance time while either request remains unresolved.

The story reports 27 focused tests passing, type-check and build succeeding, a controlled browser smoke, and a separate backend-envelope check. These reports do not resolve the uncovered pending-request deadline case.
actionable_items: Enforce the recovery deadline while task-status and calculation requests are pending. On expiry, stop animation, retain usable rows, expose retry, and prevent expired responses from changing the displayed result; do not assume backend work was cancelled.
Add controlled-time regressions that advance time while task-status and recalculation requests remain unresolved. Verify deadline termination, rejection of late responses, and retry behavior.

post_implementation_reviews.reason: The prior deadline gap is addressed: each recovery cycle starts an independent five-minute alarm, and expiry abandons that cycle so pending responses cannot update the displayed result. The regressions cover stalled task-status reads, stalled recalculations, and stalled retry requests, including retaining cached rows, stopping the provisional state, exposing retry, and ignoring late responses. The prepared lifecycle test file is present and meaningful. The supplied evaluator evidence supports the remaining criteria and verification; no CI result is required for this review.
evidence: Inspected useCraftingProfit.ts: recovery starts a single budget alarm; expiry records a timeout and abandons the cycle; response application checks both request and active cycle identifiers.

Inspected regressions for unanswered task-status, recalculation, and retry requests. They advance the controlled clock to the deadline, verify retained rows and retry state, then resolve the late response and verify it does not change the display.
The lifecycle tests also cover provisional and pending responses, successive refresh tasks, context correlation, failure handling, and cumulative recovery budget.

The supplied evaluator reports the focused tests, type-check, build, controlled browser smoke, and separate backend-envelope connection check, and distinguishes these from real-data timing and later CI verification.
